messages:
Alex: ran a set of nsys+perfetto traces against the replay cluster. seeing two recurring spikes on cold paths: a Triton/JIT compile hotpath (large single-op compile pauses) and a kernel_selector churn that leads to kernel cache misses. uploading traces to S3: s3://redwood-perf/1850032100/nsys.tar.gz

infra-bot: nsys job finished and artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/1850032100/nsys.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

Maria: any quick numbers? short note: compile spikes usually line up with first token batches after a KV cache miss.

Ryan: can you paste the exact nsys command and the workload params (model / seqlen / batch)? also perfetto link when ready.

Alex: command I ran:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run --trace=cuda,cuda_nvtx --sample=none \
  python -m perf.run_replay --model redwood-open-3b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --warmup 0
```
Workload: redwood-open-3b, seq=2048, variable prompt lengths, steady QPS ~12.
Observed compile times: cold median ~180ms, 95th ~420ms; cached compile 8–15ms. The big ones coincide with KV-cache misses and then multiple kernel_selector lookups.

Eva: interesting. are we seeing a lot of unique shape keys? variable seqlens will blow up the compile key cardinality. also did you check kernel_cache config (size/eviction)?

Alex: kernel cache was default 1024 entries. churn looked insane — ~12k evicts during 30m run. config snippet: 
```
runtime.kernel_cache.max_entries=1024
runtime.kernel_cache.eviction_policy=LRU
```

Maria: 1024 is too small for mixed-length traffic. each (n_head, seq_len, dtype, algo) combo is its own key for Triton compiles. For long-tailed seqlen distributions we should either normalize shapes or increase cache.

Ryan: propose: (A) add compile-coalescing window (250ms) to batch similar compile requests, (B) bump kernel_cache to 8192 on staging and re-run, (C) record per-key histogram to find top-K shapes to prime. thoughts?

Alex: ran a quick experiment: cache=8192 + compile_coalesce=250ms. Results: cold median dropped to ~90ms, evicts down to ~800 in same timeframe. still seeing occasional ~120ms pauses when a KV miss triggers back-to-back kernel_selector passes. perfetto timeline: https://perfetto.local/trace/1850032100

Maria: can you share the flame view? do the long pauses show compilation or NVTX markers?

Alex: timeline shows NVTX spans pinned to "jit_compile" and a separate span for "kernel_select" that does a linear scan across candidate kernels. two sequential selects happen for some fused ops which doubles the latency.

Eva: sounds like kernel_selector may be doing full candidate enumeration per op. we should short-circuit when the throughput delta between top candidates is <5% or when existing compiled variant satisfies correctness with minor padding. cheap heuristic could cut selection time drastically.

Ryan: also think about priming: on model load, sample recent traffic (or use static histogram) and precompile top-10 shapes. trade-off is memory, but it reduces cold-start jitter.

Alex: agree. actionable plan I'm writing down: 
1) increase kernel_cache to 8192 on staging and run 1h replay (Ryan)
2) implement kernel_selector short-circuit heuristic where throughput delta <5% -> pick existing variant (Maria)
3) enable compile_coalesce=250ms in runtime (Ryan/Alex)
4) add model-load primer to compile top-K shapes (investigate perf/mem tradeoffs) (follow-up)

Maria: I'll own (2). will file a PR to add the short-circuit and unit tests. ETA EOD Friday.

Ryan: I'll schedule the staging replay tomorrow 10:00 and attach the new nsys+perfetto traces.

infra-bot: deploy job queued (#5821) for the kernel_selector PR branch.

Alex: quick config dump I used for the successful run:
```
runtime.kernel_cache.max_entries=8192
runtime.compile.coalesce_ms=250
runtime.kernel_selector.heuristics.enabled=true
```

Eva: one more note — KV cache behavior: if a KV miss forces a full context recompute we should prioritize KV prefetch/approximate hits (prefix caching) to avoid compiles during the first token. maybe add a lightweight prefix cache hit-fastpath.

Alex: good suggestion — adding prefix priming to the backlog.

Maria: PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/421 (short-circuit + tests) :sparkles:

Ryan: I'll post the staging trace when the replay completes. thanks all :thumbsup:

Alex: thanks — adding summary to the perf board and marking follow-ups. :memo:
